title: Insert common prompts in the dashboard terminal

intentCoverage.report:
Caught.

Story: SEED-298#insert-common-prompts-in-the-dashboard-terminal, `.planning/seeds/SEED-298-insert-common-prompts-in-the-dashboard-terminal.md#insert-common-prompts-in-the-dashboard-terminal` at revision `39c075087d4b0ecfc9f6510252c41feec77f334b`.

Promise: choosing a preset inserts the literal reply without Enter, so the developer edits and sends deliberately.

Fault: in `dashboard/src/TerminalPrompts.tsx`, the fixed-phrase choice callback called `insert("\r")` immediately after its existing `insert(text)`. Fixtures and assertions were unchanged. The isolated detached scratch checkout began clean at the selected revision and received its own locked npm ci installation.

Focused command, unchanged for baseline, fault and restoration:
`caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard -- --project=chromium --workers=1 dashboard/tests/terminals/session-terminal-prompts.spec.ts --grep 'desktop.*common prompts'`

Fixture: `openTerminalVoice` launches real test sessions through the maintained dashboard journey. Selected test: desktop / common prompts insert literal editable input and require deliberate Enter. Every run selected exactly one test, as recorded by the maintained proof reporter.

Baseline passed. The fault run reached `session-terminal-prompts.spec.ts:69`: the traffic assertion filtering CR/LF expected zero entries before deliberate Enter and received one carriage return. Earlier literal-phrase, menu closure and focus observations had completed, so this is the intended preset path and no-Enter assertion. Restoring the exact original bytes produced a clean Git state and a passing rerun. The owned scratch worktree was then removed; execution code was never modified by this probe.

Evidence: `/tmp/seed298-ic-baseline.json`, `/tmp/seed298-ic-fault.json`, `/tmp/seed298-ic-restored.json`; fault log and original-byte backup under `/var/folders/65/16p4k5qj42qg7l46k2j0nhj40000gn/T/dough-intent-SEED298-m8dwooa5/`.
